question: Will the 2026 Eastern Pacific hurricane season's accumulated cyclone energy exceed 350 units as of October 29, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Total is ~343.1 as of Oct 18 (Wikipedia; CSU page blocked to me). Trudy is weakening fast from 85 kt and should add only ~2-3 more units, leaving ~345-346. NHC gives a disturbance south of Central America a 90% 7-day formation chance, with a tropical depression expected midweek (~Oct 21-22) on a W-WNW track over open water. Reaching 350 needs ~4-6 units from it by Oct 29, i.e. ~6 days at moderate tropical-storm strength, or fewer if it becomes a hurricane. Risks: late or weak development, formation slipping, CSU total lower than Wikipedia's. No market found.
calls.dossier:
- Resolves off the 'Current Season Northeast Pacific Ocean ACE' total on the CSU Realtime page (fallback: Climatlas), read Oct 29 2026; must be >350.0. The CSU page returned 403 to this researcher, so its exact current value is unverified.
- Event window: season-to-date cumulative through the Oct 29 read; as of Oct 19 02:30Z about 10.6 days remain.
- Reported total history: ACE 318.8 when the 2018 record (318.1) was passed in mid-Oct (Swellnet, Oct 14); 331 as of Oct 15 (Yale Climate Connections); ~336.7 Oct 16 (question background); 343.1 on Wikipedia (~Oct 18), split as Eastern Pacific 235.0 + Central Pacific 108.1. That suggests the combined figure is the comparable one, though the question's fine print says 'east of 140W' (ambiguity).
- Trudy: peaked as a Cat 3 (120 mph) ~Oct 16, fell to Cat 1 Oct 17, back to Cat 2 Oct 18 (100-105 mph at 12Z). NHC TWD 2205Z Oct 18: 85 kt, 974 mb, moving NW at 5 kt near 19.5N 107.0W; 'rapid weakening is expected to begin tonight', could become post-tropical as early as late Tue Oct 20, dissipating Thu Oct 22. Rough remaining ACE from a rapid-decay profile: ~2-3 units.
- NHC TWO 5 PM PDT Oct 18: low pressure well south of Guatemala/El Salvador; 20% in 48h, 90% in 7 days; TD expected 'around the middle of this week' moving W-WNW well offshore; conditions conducive to gradual development.
- Climatology (Yale CC): a typical NE Pacific season produces ~2 more named storms incl. 1 major hurricane from Oct 15 onward; this is an El Nino year, and 2026 has 22 named storms, 12 hurricanes, 9 majors.
- ACE arithmetic: one 6-hour fix at 35/45/65/85 kt = 0.12/0.20/0.42/0.72 units. Roughly 4-6 units are needed beyond Trudy's remainder; e.g. ~24 fixes averaging ~50 kt, or ~2-3 days at hurricane strength.
- Counter-evidence: Trudy underperformed its Cat 4 forecast, possibly because earlier storms left cooler upwelled water; a system forming ~Oct 21-22 has only ~7 days before the read; the CSU value could differ from Wikipedia's.
- Markets: none found on Polymarket, Manifold or Kalshi.
- Searched but not found: the exact CSU per-storm table, Trudy's per-storm ACE, the NHC intensity forecast table, model intensity guidance for the new disturbance.

calls.reasoning: aceofcanes shows the E+C Pacific season total at 343.1 as of Oct 19 00Z, so it already includes Trudy's Oct 18 85-kt fixes; Run 3's extra 4-5 units were double-counted. NHC's latest forecast weakens Trudy 80->65->50->40 kt and makes it post-tropical by Oct 21 06Z, about 2.5-2.8 more ACE, so Trudy alone ends the season near 345.5-346. Crossing 350 needs ~4-5 units from the new low south of Central America (20% in 48h, 90% in 7 days, TD expected midweek, 'gradual' development). It would need ~4-5 named-storm days averaging ~50 kt, or a brief hurricane phase, before the Oct 29 read. P(named in time) ~0.7 x P(>=4.5 units | named) ~0.5-0.55, plus a small allowance for other systems, gives ~0.38. No human market found.
calls.reconciliation: Main factual dispute: the timestamp of the 343.1 total. aceofcanes.com gives 343.1 as of Oct 19 00:00 UTC (Trudy at 12.6), so Run 3's +4-5 for Oct 18 is double-counted. Runs 1 and 2's ~343 baseline is correct. NHC TCD advisory 22 (18/21Z) intensity forecast: 85, 80, 65, 50, 40 kt, then post-tropical by 21/06Z, implying ~2.5-2.8 more ACE from Trudy (Run 1 said 2-3, Run 2 said 1-3, both consistent). The NHC TWO (Oct 18 5 PM PDT) confirmed 20%/90% and 'gradual development' with a TD around midweek. Wikipedia's combined 343.1 (EPac 235.0 + CPac 108.1) matches the question's own 336.7 baseline series, so the CSU 'Northeast Pacific' figure is the combined one. The CSU page itself returned 403, so CSU's exact value is unverified. What remains is a judgment: whether the new system adds ~4.5 units within ~6-7 days of genesis. I put that near 0.5 conditional on naming, which gives about 0.38, below Runs 1 and 2 because the gap is ~4-5 units rather than Run 1's lower end, and Trudy's decay is front-loaded.
